business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 Business section.
business_model.claim: American Tower's primary business is leasing space on communications sites (towers, DAS networks, data centers) to wireless service providers, broadcast companies, wireless data providers, government agencies, municipalities, and other tenants.

business_model.claim: The company reports results in six segments: U.S. & Canada property, Africa & APAC property, Europe property, Latin America property, Data Centers, and Services.

business_model.claim: Property operations accounted for 97% of total revenues in 2025 and 98% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026; services operations accounted for 3% in 2025.

Our property operations, which accounted for 98% and 98% of our total revenues for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K MD&A, Property Operations Revenue Growth section.
business_model.claim: Revenue growth is driven by three primary factors: new colocations and lease amendments, contractual rent escalations on existing leases net of churn, and revenue from newly acquired or constructed sites.
quotes: The primary factors affecting the revenue growth of our property segments are: •Growth in tenant billings, including: •New revenue attributable to leasing additional space on our sites ("colocations") and lease amendments; •Contractual rent escalations on existing tenant leases, net of churn; and •New revenue attributable to leases in place on day one on sites acquired or constructed since the beginning of the prior-year period.

business_model.claim: U.S. tenant leases carry a fixed annual escalation averaging approximately 3%; most international markets use an inflationary index or a combination of fixed and index-based escalators.
quotes: with provisions that periodically increase the rent due under the lease, typically annually, based on a fixed escalation percentage (averaging approximately 3% in the United States) or an inflationary index in most of our international markets, or a combination of both.

business_model.claim: As of December 31, 2025, the company expected to generate over $54 billion of non-cancellable tenant lease revenue over future periods; by September 30, 2026, this figure had decreased to nearly $49 billion.
quotes: Based upon foreign currency exchange rates and the tenant leases in place as of December 31, 2025, we expect to generate over $54 billion of non-cancellable tenant lease revenue over future periods, before the impact of straight-line lease accounting.

Based upon existing customer leases and foreign currency exchange rates as of September 30, 2026, we expect to generate nearly $49 billion of non-cancellable customer lease revenue over future periods, before the impact of straight-line lease accounting.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1, Property Operations section.
business_model.claim: Direct operating costs of property segments consist primarily of ground rent, power and fuel costs, property taxes, and repairs and maintenance; some or all of ground rent and power/fuel may be passed through to tenants.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1, under 'High operating margins.'

quotes: AT&T Mexico, which represented approximately $300 million of tenant revenue in 2025, is challenging the calculation of the monthly lease amount established under our Master Lease Agreement with AT&T Mexico (the "MLA"), as well as certain other provisions of the MLA, seeking rent abatement both retroactively and prospectively

risks.basis: Stated in P4 (10-Q MD&A) and P1 (10-K Business); the company directly attributes the increase to DISH.
risks.claim: Tenant billings churn rose to approximately 5% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, driven primarily by DISH, compared to approximately 2% for the full year ended December 31, 2025, signaling a material deterioration in the recurring-revenue thesis.
quotes: During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, churn was approximately 5% of our tenant billings, primarily driven by churn due to one of our U.S. customers, DISH Wireless L.L.C., a subsidiary of DISH Network Corporation ("DISH") in our U.S. & Canada property segment, as discussed below. Beginning on January 1, 2026, 100% of DISH revenue has been reflected in churn.
During the year ended December 31, 2025, churn was approximately 2% of our tenant billings, primarily driven by churn in our U.S. & Canada property segment.

risks.basis: Stated in P1 (10-K Business, as of Dec 31, 2025) and P4 (10-Q MD&A, as of Sep 30, 2026); both are company-reported forward-looking figures.
risks.claim: Non-cancellable customer lease revenue declined from over $54 billion as of December 31, 2025 to nearly $49 billion as of September 30, 2026, a reduction of approximately $5 billion in nine months, reflecting divestitures and the DISH termination.
quotes: Based upon foreign currency exchange rates and the tenant leases in place as of December 31, 2025, we expect to generate over $54 billion of non-cancellable tenant lease revenue over future periods, before the impact of straight-line lease accounting.

Based upon existing customer leases and foreign currency exchange rates as of September 30, 2026, we expect to generate nearly $49 billion of non-cancellable customer lease revenue over future periods, before the impact of straight-line lease accounting.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (10-K Risk Factors) as a company-identified risk; the counterarguments are drawn from P1 (10-K Business) and P5 (8-K earnings release).
risks.claim: New technologies including satellite communications, RAN sharing, and AI-driven network efficiency could reduce demand for tower-based wireless services and data center space, threatening the long-term growth premise.
quotes: technological changes, including artificial intelligence ("AI"), wireless equipment changes, satellite technology and an increase in the use of radio access network ("RAN") sharing among wireless service providers

extensive sharing of site infrastructure through RAN sharing, roaming or resale arrangements among wireless service providers, including due to increases in advanced network technology such as 5G, as an alternative to leasing our communications sites, without compensation to us, may cause new lease activity to slow if carriers utilize shared equipment rather than deploy new equipment

the development and implementation of new technologies designed to enhance the efficiency of wireless networks or changes in a customer's business model could reduce the need for tower-based wireless services, decrease demand for tower space or reduce previously obtainable lease rates
